title_ar: الدرس الرابع من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية
title_en: The fourth lesson of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares
body_ar:
الكاتب : الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو الدرس الاول من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية التي قام بها الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو فى مركز تكوين العلماء

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

وعدناكم في نهاية الدرس الماضي بإجابة أسئلتكم فلعلنا نبدأ بها إن شاء الله تعالى في هذه الليلة، ومن الأسئلة التي جاءت عبر الموقع من العالم: ذكر في أقسام المطلقة القسم الرابع وهو المطلقة طلاقا بائنا في صحة أو مرض غير مخوف أنها ترث سواء كانت في العدة أم لا؟
body_en:
Author: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew. The first lesson of the lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares, given by Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

We promised you at the end of the last lesson that we would answer your questions, so let us perhaps begin with them, God Most High willing, this evening. Among the questions that have come in through the website from around the world: in the categories of the divorced woman, the fourth category was mentioned — the woman irrevocably divorced while [the husband was] in health, or in an illness not to be feared — that she inherits whether she is within the waiting period or not?

flags.arabic: الدرس الرابع … / … الدرس الاول من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية
flags.context: the page title says 'the fourth lesson'; the byline immediately below it says 'the first lesson'
options: keep both as served, flag, and withhold the lesson number from any ordering of the course
treat the title as correct and the byline as the CMS error
treat the byline as correct and the title as the CMS error
flags.note: TITLE/BODY MISMATCH — source defect, not to be fixed unilaterally. The body's own content settles that it is not the first lesson: it opens 'we promised you at the end of the last lesson', which a first lesson cannot say. So the byline is wrong and the title may be right, but the byline is the same boilerplate the CMS repeats across this series and cannot be relied on either way. The same defect appears at id 625. Until the Sheikh's office confirms the true sequence, the lesson numbers in this series should not be used to order the course on the site.

flags.arabic: المطلقة طلاقا بائنا في صحة أو مرض غير مخوف أنها ترث سواء كانت في العدة أم لا؟
flags.context: the question the lesson opens with; the published text stops here and the answer is not given
options: withhold from display as a teaching text until the full transcript behind the .docx download is obtained
display with a prominent banner marking that the answer is not published
display the excerpt as it stands
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The excerpt ends on the question mark. The question concerns whether a woman irrevocably divorced outside a final illness inherits from her former husband — a point on which the schools differ and which has direct consequences for an estate. The reader is given the question and no answer at all. The full transcript is behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link.

flags.arabic: في صحة أو مرض غير مخوف
flags.context: the circumstances of the irrevocable divorce
options: while [the husband was] in health, or in an illness not to be feared
in a state of health, or in a non-terminal illness
during health or during an illness that gives no cause for alarm
flags.note: The subject of 'health' is not expressed in the Arabic and has been supplied in brackets: the doctrine concerns the husband's condition at the time he pronounces the divorce, because a divorce in the final illness (maraḍ al-mawt) is treated as an attempt to exclude the wife from the estate. Maraḍ ghayr mukhawwif is the technical opposite of that — an illness from which death is not feared. 'Non-terminal' in option 1 is a modern medical term and imports a different test.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text consists of the opening formula of the lesson and the first question, then breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'The Centre for the Formation of Scholars' renders Markaz Takwīn al-ʿUlamāʾ, the Sheikh's institute in Nouakchott. The Arabic name should be kept alongside the English on the site, as the institute is known by it.
The opening doxology (khuṭbat al-ḥājah) is translated rather than omitted, since it is part of the transcript as published.
